newsitem.title: GERMANY: German units welcome Cordiant demerger.
newsitem.headline: German units welcome Cordiant demerger.

text.p: The decision by London-based advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc to demerge into three independently managed businesses was welcomed on Tuesday by two of its German ad units.
Directors of agencies Bates and Scholz & Friends said the Cordiant dissolution would lead to stronger growth by freeing them to compete and respond to client needs more effectively.

"Our customers never really saw the necessity of a holding" said Ulrich Veigel, managing director of Bates's German unit. "Bates was obstructed from dealing with big Saatchi & Saatchi customers like Procter & Gamble or its competitors."

Cordiant, the holding company formerly known as Saatchi & Saatchi, announced on Monday it planned to split into three firms: Saatchi & Saatchi, Bates and Zenith. Several large customers welcomed the decision.
"The long overdue restructuring opens new business opportunities and allows us to increase our influence over Bates," said Norbert Lindhof, managing director of Hamburg-based Scholz & Friends.
Cordiant owns 90 percent of Scholz & Friends, which will become a unit of the Bates group. Lindhof said he did not know if the firm's chief executive, Peter Schoening, would join the Bates board.
Saatchi & Saatchi GmbH in Frankfurt could not be reached for comment.
Lindhof said he expected a 10-percent increase in turnover for Scholz & Friends in the current year. The company has opened a new Singapore office and plans to expand with a new agency in Rome.
Industry sources said Scholz & Friends posted 85 million marks in turnover in 1996, 11 percent more than in 1995.
Bates's Veigel predicted the break with Saatchi & Saatchi would have even more positive effects for Bates Germany GmbH than it would internationally.

"As probably the only international agency network in Germany, 90 percent of Bates Germany's customers are German," Veigel said. He predicted five percent growth for the current year, matching the rate for 1996.

Bates's German unit's largest customers include Eurocard, DG Bank and the Oetker dairy products brand Landliebe. Bates has pitched for the accounts of foods brand Langnese and 4711 perfumes and aftershaves.

Scholz & Friends, one of the 10 largest German ad groups, represents the accounts of Tchibo coffees, Reemtsma tobacco, luxury auto maker BMW, Deutsche Bank, computer company Compaq and Apollinaris beverages.
